paper.title: Tsallis-INF: An Optimal Algorithm for Stochastic and Adversarial Bandits

unmapped: performance measured by pseudo-regret against best arm in expectation
settings.definition_quote: In the (\emph{adaptive}) \emph{adversarial setting}, the adversary selects the losses arbitrarily, potentially based on the history of the agent's actions $(I_1,\dots,I_{t-1})$ and the adversary's own internal randomization.

settings.name_in_paper: adversarial regime with a (Delta, C, T) self-bounding constraint
unmapped: self-bounding constraint: Reg_T >= sum_t sum_i Delta_i P(I_t=i) - C at time T; includes stochastic, stochastically constrained adversarial and corrupted stochastic regimes
settings.definition_quote: We further define an \emph{adversarial regime with a $(\Delta, C, T)$ self-bounding constraint}, where $\Delta\in[0,1]^K$ and $C\geq 0$. In this regime, the adversary selects losses such that at time $T$ the regret of any algorithm satisfies \Reg \geq \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_i \Delta_i \mathbb{P}(I_t = i) - C.

unmapped: stochastically constrained adversary: fixed expected gaps between arms, means may change over time and depend on past actions
settings.definition_quote: In this setting, the losses $\ell_{t,i}$ are drawn from distributions with fixed gaps, $\E[\ell_{t,i} - \ell_{t,j}] = \tilde \Delta_{i,j}$ independently of $t$, but the means, as well as other parameters of the distributions of all arms, are allowed to change with time and may depend on the agent's past actions.

settings.name_in_paper: stochastically constrained adversarial environment with adversarial corruptions
unmapped: underlying environment is stochastically constrained adversarial (not only i.i.d.)
corruption is adaptive, measured as sum_t ||bar l_t - l_t||_inf <= C
settings.definition_quote: Let $\overline{\mathcal{L}}_T$ be a sequence of losses generated by a stochastically constrained adversary with best arm $i^*$ and gaps $\AnyGap$, and let $\mathcal{L}_T$ be its adaptively corrupted version with corruption amount bounded by $C$.

unmapped: utility-based: P[W_t=I_t]=(1+u_{I_t}-u_{J_t})/2; regret = sum_t 2u_{i*} - u_{I_t} - u_{J_t}
settings.definition_quote: The problem is defined by $K$ arms with utilities $u_i\in [0,1]$. At each round, an agent has to select two arms, $I_t$ and $J_t$, to ``duel''. The feedback is the winner $W_t$ of the ``duel'', which is chosen according to $\mathbb{P}[W_t=I_t] = \frac{1+u_{I_t}-u_{J_t}}{2}$.

unmapped: time-dependent utilities u_{t,i} chosen by adversary; regret against best fixed utility in hindsight
settings.definition_quote: In the adversarial version of the problem, the utilities $u_i$ are not constant but time dependent, $u_{t,i}$, and selected by an adversary.
